slides.title: Handling Blocking Functions in AsyncIO
slides.prompt: Blocking I/O or heavy CPU work freezes the event loop. Use `asyncio.to_thread()` (Python 3.9+) or `loop.run_in_executor()` to delegate synchronous tasks to a thread/process pool.
slides.codeSnippet:
import asyncio
import time

def blocking_cpu_task(n):
    time.sleep(1) # Synchronous blocking call
    return n * n

async def main():
    # Offload to background thread pool (Python 3.9+)
    result = await asyncio.to_thread(blocking_cpu_task, 5)
    print(result)

slides.title: Consequences of Blocking the Event Loop
slides.prompt: What happens when a synchronous blocking function (like `time.sleep(5)`) is executed directly inside an async coroutine without offloading?
options: The entire event loop freezes and stalls all other concurrent tasks for 5 seconds
AsyncIO automatically spawns a thread to handle the blocking call
Python raises a BlockingIOError at runtime
The event loop cancels the blocking coroutine
slides.correctAnswer: The entire event loop freezes and stalls all other concurrent tasks for 5 seconds
